gloss: the curtain rises; to begin; to get underway

definitions.explanation: Literal use: the stage curtain goes up at the start of a play, concert, or similar performance.

definitions.gloss: to begin; to get underway; to open (of a major event or era)
definitions.explanation: Figurative use: a significant event, era, or contest begins — a tournament, a new political era, a project, a campaign. Carries a ceremonial or dramatic tone, framing the beginning as a public unfolding.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会場|かいじょう}→会場：01269_kaijou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{照明|しょうめい}→照明：03243_shoumei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{落|お}ち→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧、⟦いよいよ→いよいよ：06353_iyoiyo⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The lights in the hall dimmed, and at last the curtain rose.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The curtain has risen on a new era.

examples.japanese: {選挙戦|せんきょせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The election campaign has gotten underway.

examples.japanese: ⟦{全国|ぜんこく}→全国：03311_zenkoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{注目|ちゅうもく}→注目：03483_chuumoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がろう⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The tournament, which has drawn attention from all over the country, is about to get underway.

notes:
Literally 'the curtain goes up', referring to the rising of a stage curtain at the start of a performance. Widely used figuratively for the dramatic opening of any large event, contest, or era.

USAGE:
- The figurative use is much more common in writing and news than the literal theatrical use.
- Often takes a noun marked by ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ as its subject: ⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる, ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる.
- Frequently appears with ⟦いよいよ→いよいよ：06353_iyoiyo⟧ ('at last'), ついに ('finally'), or ようやく for dramatic effect.
- The opposite is ⟦{幕|まく}→幕：12518_maku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{下|お}りる ('the curtain falls') or ⟦{幕|まく}を{閉|と}じる→幕を閉じる：17332_makuwotojiru⟧ ('to close; to come to an end'), used for conclusions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる: the tournament gets underway
- ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる: a new era begins
- ⟦いよいよ→いよいよ：06353_iyoiyo⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる: the curtain is about to rise at last
- {選挙戦|せんきょせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる: the election campaign gets underway

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{幕|まく}→幕：12518_maku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{下|お}りる: the curtain falls — the direct opposite, used when something ends.
- ⟦{幕|まく}→幕：12518_maku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧: to open the curtain; to begin an event — transitive counterpart; used when someone officially opens an event.
- ⟦{開幕|かいまく}→開幕：08174_kaimaku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to open; to start (of a season or event) — a more compact noun-verb with similar meaning; very common in sports reporting.
- ⟦{始|はじ}まる→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧: to begin — the plain, everyday verb without the dramatic framing.
